# The Bet · FinWise

> Module 1 · Ignite a PLG Motion. The growth hypothesis and where you're betting, plus the growth-loop visualization.

## Growth hypothesis

FinWise's biggest growth problem is FinWise is losing more customers than it gains every month., because Most customers use FinWise alone, so it never becomes part of how their business runs day to day..

_Working notes: I think FinWise's biggest problem is that paying customers don't keep seeing value from the product, so most of them leave within a year. 

Evidence: 
1. 60% of paying customers churn within a year, so FinWise loses most of the customers it works hard to win.
2. Spending more on acquisition isn't driving growth, because new customers leave about as fast as they join.
3. Small businesses may only use finance tools occasionally, so they can forget the value between uses. Against the data: In all 13 months, more customers left than joined: 317 left, 128 joined, a net loss of 189. It also got worse over time, with 115 leaving in the first 6 months and 173 in the last 6.

_____

## The bet

Encourage customers to invite their accountant or a teammate, then compare whether shared accounts stay longer and pay more often than solo accounts.

**Not doing:** I'm not going after more website visitors or trials, because bringing more people in doesn't help if most don't pay and the ones who do end up leaving.

_____

## Growth loop

**Loop type:** Collaboration, If customers invite their accountant or business partner into FinWise, it becomes a tool the whole business relies on, and that makes it harder to quit. This can help keep customers and get more trial users to pay.
